section_summary.extract_value: This section, titled 'Socio-demographic factors and dependent variables', discusses how various demographic factors relate to depression and loneliness in a single sample of 465 participants. It reports significant sex differences in loneliness (women lonelier), marital status differences (widows more depressed and lonelier), education differences in loneliness (primary school education associated with more loneliness), and family type differences in loneliness (polygamous families reported higher loneliness). Unemployed participants were also found to be more depressed and lonelier. No age differences were found for either depression or loneliness, and bereavement was not significant for either outcome.
